findings.documented: Pass API key as query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXX
findings.actual: API key must be sent as a request header: X-API-Key: IVY26-XXXX. Passing it as a query parameter returns HTTP 401 with message: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'
findings.how_found: First curl call with query param returned 401 with explicit error message
findings.impact: Any client following the documentation cannot authenticate at all

findings.documented: Response token field is 'token'. Token valid for 86400 seconds (24 hours). 'There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: Response field is 'access_token' (not 'token'). expires_in is 900 seconds (15 minutes, not 24 hours). Response also includes 'refresh_token' and 'refresh_url: /auth/refresh'. A refresh flow exists and is required.
findings.how_found: Inspected login response JSON — field names and expiry differ from docs. refresh_token and refresh_url present in response.
findings.impact: Critical: clients storing 'token' field get undefined. 15-min expiry means sessions expire quickly without implementing the undocumented refresh flow.

findings.documented: Endpoint not mentioned. Documentation states there is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts {refresh_token: '...'} with X-API-Key header. Returns a new access_token and refresh_token.
findings.how_found: Login response included refresh_url field pointing to /auth/refresh. Confirmed by calling the endpoint successfully.
findings.impact: Without implementing refresh, frontend sessions expire after 15 minutes. The endpoint is entirely undocumented.

findings.documented: Pagination uses 'page' (1-indexed) and 'limit' (max 200). Response shape: {total, page, page_size, results}
findings.actual: Pagination uses 'offset' (0-indexed) and 'limit' (max 50, not 200). Response shape: {total, limit, offset, count, has_more, results}. Requesting limit=200 silently returns 50 records.
findings.how_found: Inspected first response — saw offset/has_more instead of page/page_size. Confirmed limit cap by requesting limit=200 and receiving 50.
findings.impact: Clients using page= parameter get first page repeatedly. Clients assuming limit=200 will miss records. 'total' field also understates actual record count (see separate finding).

findings.documented: total field is the exact number of records matching filters
findings.actual: total=3572 reported but 3800 records are actually retrievable by paginating to the end. The total field understates the real count by 228 records.
findings.how_found: Paginated all the way through with has_more flag — collected 3800 records despite total saying 3572.
findings.impact: Clients computing page count from total will stop early and miss 228 records

findings.documented: Returns only active listings. 'Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side'
findings.actual: Returns all listings including those with is_live=false. 802 of 3800 retrieved records have is_live=false.
findings.how_found: Found is_live=false records in the response. The field exists on every listing object.
findings.impact: Clients should filter is_live client-side before showing to users

findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{id} returns 404. The correct path is GET /v1/listings/{id} (plural, matching the collection endpoint).
findings.impact: Any client using the documented path cannot fetch individual listings

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings
findings.actual: Returns HTTP 404. Endpoint does not exist.
findings.impact: 'You may also like' feature cannot be built as documented

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for the city
findings.actual: Returns HTTP 404. Endpoint does not exist.
findings.impact: Insights/dashboard screen must compute aggregates from raw data instead

findings.actual: GET /v1/favourites returns 404. The endpoint path or spelling may differ. Requires further investigation.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/favourites with valid auth, received 404.
findings.impact: Saved listings feature cannot be implemented as documented

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in Indian rupees (integer)
findings.actual: price_min values appear to be in lakhs (e.g. 80.0 = ₹80 lakhs) and price_max values appear to be in crores (e.g. 3.22 = ₹3.22 crores). Values are floating-point, not integers. Cross-referencing P30001: doc price_min=80, actual listing prices ~₹72-91 lakhs; doc price_max=3.22, which as crores correctly bounds the listings.
findings.how_found: Noticed price_min=80.0 and price_max=3.22 — impossible if both rupees since min > max. Cross-referenced with actual listing prices for the same project.
findings.impact: Displaying raw values as rupees would show e.g. ₹3 instead of ₹3.22 Cr — completely wrong prices to users

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: 27 listings describe physically impossible properties: price=0, floor > total_floors, carpet area > super built-up area, or 0-bedroom apartments.
findings.how_found: Scanned all 3800 listings for logical impossibilities in numeric fields.
findings.impact: These should be excluded from price calculations and not shown to users

findings.documented: posted_by_contact is the seller's verified contact number
findings.actual: 283 listings are posted by 10 phone numbers each associated with 20-31 listings across multiple unrelated localities. A legitimate agent/owner does not simultaneously hold 20-31 properties across Pune. These are bulk-posted fake listings designed to generate enquiries.
findings.how_found: Counted listings per contact number. Normal distribution peaks at 1-4. Contacts with 20+ listings in unrelated localities are statistically anomalous.
findings.impact: Users contacting these numbers will reach fraudsters, not real sellers

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: 285 listings share an exact lat/lng coordinate with another listing. Same apartment building listed multiple times on different websites at different prices for different bedroom counts — these represent the same physical property.
findings.how_found: Grouped all 3800 listings by (latitude, longitude) — found 247 coordinate groups containing more than one listing.
findings.impact: 3800 total records describe only 3515 distinct physical properties

findings.documented: total_listings is the number of listings currently available in the project. It is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: 317 of 414 projects (76%) have a total_listings value that disagrees with the actual count of listings in the dataset. E.g. P30003: reports 7, actual 4; P30008: reports 0, actual 4.
findings.how_found: Counted listings per project_id across all 3800 listing records and compared to project.total_listings.
findings.impact: Project cards showing listing counts mislead users about property availability

findings.documented: Returns service status and the server clock
findings.actual: Returns {status, server_time, timezone, reference_date}. server_time carries an explicit +05:30 IST offset (not UTC/Z). Also returns the reference_date field (2026-09-10T00:00:00+05:30) which is not mentioned in the documentation.
findings.how_found: Called /health before writing any other code — first endpoint tested
findings.impact: Low — server_time is informational. reference_date is a useful undocumented field.
